hypothesis: If the claim holds, the measured free surface of a healthy biconcave red blood cell in plasma or isotonic buffer has non-constant mean curvature (the dimple has negative mean curvature and the rim has positive), and when the cell is swollen in hypotonic medium it becomes a sphere, which is a constant-mean-curvature surface.
pass_criterion: For at least 30 reconstructed 3D discocyte surfaces in isotonic medium, after smoothing, the mean curvature H sampled over the non-rim surface has a coefficient of variation above 0.5. H must also change sign between the dimple centre and the rim in at least 90% of cells. The same cells (or a matched set) in hypotonic medium must have a median sphericity index above 0.95 and a coefficient of variation of H below 0.15.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if the isotonic discocytes have a coefficient of variation of H of 0.2 or lower, or lack a sign change of H in more than 10% of cells. Equivalently, the claim is refuted if the surface is within measurement error of a constant-mean-curvature (Delaunay or unduloid-type) surface. It is also refuted if hypotonic cells fail to approach a sphere (median sphericity 0.95 or lower).
interpretation: Thompson's 'surface of equilibrium' under surface tension alone corresponds, for a fluid drop with a pressure difference, to a closed surface of constant mean curvature (Laplace–Young condition). The test is therefore geometric: compute the mean curvature field of measured 3D red blood cell surfaces. Modern reinterpretation: Thompson's 'some other force' (osmotic inequilibrium, fluid-crystal forces) corresponds today to membrane bending elasticity (Helfrich model) plus the spectrin cytoskeleton, with a fixed area-to-volume ratio. This test checks only the negative claim (the shape is not CMC) and the sphere-in-dilute-medium observation. It does not test which alternative force is responsible.
no_dataset_reason: I could not verify, within this session, any specific public dataset of 3D red blood cell surface reconstructions (holotomography, confocal or scanning-probe meshes) that is tied to a stable landing URL or DOI, with matched isotonic and hypotonic conditions. Under hard rule 1 I will not guess an identifier. Candidate sources such as Zenodo or figshare deposits from quantitative phase imaging papers need to be located and checked before they can be pre-registered.
